title: Make the export check pass on Windows without hiding real changes

blocks.text: The warehouse service exports stock levels as CSV every night, and a test compares the export with an expected file kept as a text block. The test passes on the Linux build agents and fails on the Windows one, with the message `line 1 differs` although the two texts look the same. A colleague's quick fix made the check ignore all white space, and a week later a row with a trailing space, which the partner's strict CSV parser rejects, went through unnoticed.
The partner's parser accepts lines ending with `\n` or `\r\n`, and a last row with or without a line break after it. Every other character counts.

items: `firstDifference(expected, actual)`: the number of the first line that differs, counting from 1, or 0 when the texts match. A line that one text has and the other doesn't is a difference.

cases.says: an export with the same text as the expected one matches
a changed value is reported with the number of its line
a row missing at the end is reported as a difference on that row's line
an export whose lines end with \r\n matches the same rows ending with \n
an export that doesn't end its last row with a line break matches one that does
a space added at the end of a row is reported as a difference on that row

origin.section: A Text Block Fixture Has `\n` Line Endings, So Compare Lines When the Format Doesn't Care

concepts: A text block fixture ends its lines with \n and has an exact final newline, so against text from a file or another program compare lines when the format ignores line endings, without ignoring other characters.
